evidence: "# Bipartite coloring"; "# bipartition via BFS coloring"
affordance_in_statement: The physical architecture of the array divides all modules into exactly two separate containment zones. The system's constraints guarantee that destructive resonance is only possible between a module in the first zone and a module in the second zone.
removal_suggestion: Replace the two-zone guarantee with a weaker statement allowing resonance links within a zone as well. Then bipartite coloring is no longer guaranteed, so a solution must handle general independent-set instances rather than directly selecting a color class.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: BFS-colors the guaranteed bipartite graph and constructs the answer from one color class
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The constraints guarantee that destructive resonance occurs only between the two zones.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses a BFS bipartition as the basis for selecting a safe set
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The physical architecture divides all modules into exactly two zones, with every reported conflict crossing the zones.

common_affordance: The explicit guarantee that the conflict graph is bipartite because every conflict crosses one of two zones

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It treats bipartite coloring as sufficient for constructing the requested set, rather than solving the general exact-size independent-set problem when that structural guarantee is absent.
It likewise bases construction on the two BFS color classes and therefore depends on the conflict graph being bipartite.

recommended_edit: Remove the guarantee that every resonance link crosses the two zones, and explicitly allow links between modules in the same zone. This single change invalidates the shared bipartite-coloring shortcut for both surviving solutions.
regression_risk: This may turn the task into a substantially harder general independent-set problem and could invalidate intended polynomial-time solutions.
